failure_summary: Run 1 alone fails A6 (pre-computed): its served prose never writes the number of the better column, wrapping only the phrase "central column" in [zone:col3], although the assembled prompt states "Better move: column 3 (lands at c3r2)" verbatim and render_decision.link.text repeats "column 3 was the better move" - correct unambiguous information the model declined to state, hence prompt_confusion (production-fidelity run on gpt-5.4-mini, so not separable from model capability).
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null (not scored, not passed). A5/A7 graded on all 5 runs against servedExplanation with markup stripped (v2 addendum). | A6 run 1 FAIL, copied verbatim from *_served_mechanical.json (note: "prose never names column 3"); runs 0,2,3,4 A6 pass. | A5b applies (player 2, boardState opening) and passes on all 5 runs: every run frames column 3 as the tougher hold/defense ("tougher central hold", "makes your defense harder to crack", "toughest defense") and none says the player is already lost. | Raw cNrM in mechanism on runs 2 and 4 is NOT charged: servedExplanation renders "at column 4, row 3" (v2 addendum, guard stripInternalTokens). | Board truth verified on render_decision.finalMovestring 215154552111000422410002234445566666633 via visualize_board.sh: row 3 cells c3r3/c4r3/c5r3/c6r3 are all X (player 1 = the opponent) and c4r3 is the winning move 39, so the window and completing cell every run names are real (G4 pass); the rendered threat list (major at c4r5 and c4r6, both players) matches the visualizer exactly (G5 pass). | G3 pass: the only shown:false boards are afterBest/afterPlayed, tag-set-identical to the near-empty decision board, and no run needed them. | G7 judgment half passes on all 5 runs: line-shaped words sit on the future:windows handle and single-square words on the future:c4r3 handle, nothing over-wrapped, annotationRepairs empty on every row. | Observation, not charged to any defined axis: the assembled prompt lists [zone:better-col] in its mandatory set, yet runs 0, 2, 3 and 4 emit no column zone at all (only run 1 does). Required-set omission has no axis in this rubric, but it is the same seam that produced the A6 failure. | Cosmetic, not an A5a violation: run 1 writes "the sideier column".

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.link.text / assembled-prompt Decision block ("Better move: column 3 (lands at c3r2)")
counterexamples.evidence: Run 1 servedExplanation names the better move only as "[zone:col3]central column[/zone:col3]" / "the more central column"; the digit 3 never appears, so a player reading the served text cannot tell which column to have played. The number is present verbatim in the assembled prompt, and every other run states it in prose, so this is a model omission, not information suppression. The same run also wraps the played column as "[zone:col2]the sideier column[/zone:col2]".
